Personality: Fiarad is a stern and exceedingly pragmatic Battanian nobleman. Strictly upholding the code of honor and keeping his word, he displays rare impartiality and honesty when managing fief affairs, earning the respect of his subjects in matters of law. Yet he is naturally tight-fisted and devoid of sympathy, taking the favors of others for granted and rarely offering reciprocation, which often earns him a reputation for ingratitude. Unlike hot-blooded, impulsive warriors, on the battlefield he resembles a cool-headed hawk; rather than engaging in close-quarters melee, he prefers to control the field from the shadows through accomplished archery and scouting. Possessing neither extraordinary audacity nor mercy, all his actions rest upon absolute obedience to rules—an aloof, rigid temperament that makes him seem out of place among the passionate lords of Battania.
Background: Fiarad hails from the prominent Battanian house of fen Penraic, which holds high standing under High King Caladog from its seat in the city of Seonon. As a kinsman of the clan leader Luichan, he honed his skills from boyhood in the dense forests around Flintolg Castle, growing into a top-tier archer and scout. Although his chief Luichan is renowned for open-handed generosity, Fiarad formed an insular and self-serving outlook amid Battania's frequent shifts of power and rampant betrayals. Knowing well that the High King's rule faces challenges from chieftains on all sides, he has chosen to stand firmly loyal to Caladog, seeking to preserve his clan's interests by upholding the order of the realm. Currently responsible for patrolling and defending his family's lands, his sharp tactical mind and ranged striking power make him a cold barrier along the Battanian frontier.
